summary_paraphrase: A nine-year-old who is always told she is too small dreams of a quest for a bravery drink; she crosses a river, finds her way and passes a frightening cave on her own ideas, wakes before drinking, and her grandmother shows her she was brave already.

characters.name: Bohlale
characters.desire: to do what her older siblings do; to become brave
characters.fear: being too small, weak and not brave enough
characters.change: from believing she needs a magic drink to seeing her own courage
characters.strengths: notices things (leaf, giraffe) and turns them into plans

characters.name: Gogo
characters.personality: believes in her; frames the night and the morning

characters.name: giraffe
characters.relation_to_protagonist: model she copies to see far

characters.name: fireflies
characters.relation_to_protagonist: the scary eyes, revealed as guides

humor_notes: Light: being as tall as a giraffe, the stretched 'good moooorning'.

repetition.description: three near-quits ('I think I will give up because…') each followed by her own idea
repetition.why: each obstacle escalates (river, lost, frightening cave) and each is solved differently, so the pattern builds rather than repeats

repetition.description: step counting the reader joins (50, 100, 200, total)
repetition.why: invites participation and carries the count across a page turn, but the arithmetic asides also interrupt the story's tension

repetition.description: Gogo's 'I believe in you' at bedtime answered by 'you ARE brave' in the morning; the not-as-wise/strong/brave list returns
repetition.why: the ending answers the exact doubt the beginning set up

notes: The bedroom is drawn twice, night with stars (p4) and sunrise (p14): the picture frames the dream.
The giraffe appears in the picture on p9 before the text needs it, planting the next solution.
The frightening eyes (p11) are drawn as glowing dots in the dark; the next page redraws them as friendly fireflies.

strengths: each obstacle is solved by the child's own observation (leaf to raft, giraffe to tree, looking again at the eyes)
bedtime frame: blessing at night, reframing in the morning; the adventure lives inside a dream
the fear peak is defused on the very next page
weaknesses: maths and comprehension asides (ages, branches, total steps) interrupt the story's tension
the narrator addresses the reader often, which flattens immersion
long for a picture book (15 story pages, longer paragraphs)

anti_patterns.note: mild: the lesson is enacted across pages 7-13, then also spoken by Gogo
arithmetic questions add explanation the story does not need

child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.
child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated

age_suitability.notes: A child alone crosses a river on a home-made raft and climbs a tall tree (inside a dream). The scary-eyes peak is research intensity 4/5 for one page, about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale, and is defused on the next page. As a model: keep the dream frame and the defusal, drop the river crossing.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
